title: Life's What You Make It
year_note: First released in Germany on 18 November 1985; the UK release was 6 January 1986, when it reached 16.

notes.made: It was one of the last songs written for The Colour of Spring, after management complained there was no obvious single. Tim Friese-Greene had a drum pattern loosely based on Kate Bush's 'Running Up That Hill' and Mark Hollis played 'Green Onions' organ over it; David Rhodes added the guitar hook. On the record Hollis plays piano, Lee Harris drums, Friese-Greene organ and Mellotron, and Martin Ditcham percussion, with Friese-Greene producing.
notes.context: Hollis had said he'd be delighted if synthesizers didn't exist, and The Colour of Spring swapped them for piano, organ and guitar. The single was a hit across Europe and got to 90 in the US for two weeks in February 1986; the album reached 8 in the UK and topped the Dutch chart.

listen_for.note: Friese-Greene's beat is a slowed, loosened 'Running Up That Hill'. Kate Bush's single had come out in August 1985.
David Rhodes, Peter Gabriel's guitarist, plays the hook that holds the track together.
Hollis plays the piano himself, under his own vocal.

leads_to.title: Green Onions
leads_to.why: What Hollis was playing over the drum pattern when the song took shape.

notes.unverified: Rafe's quote credits 'Tim Friese-Greene's piano riff'. The album credits list Mark Hollis on piano for this track and Friese-Greene on organ and Mellotron; Friese-Greene brought the drum pattern.

culture.title: UK number 16
culture.line: Out in Germany on 18 November 1985 and in the UK on 6 January 1986, where it reached 16. It got to 90 in the US and charted again on a 1990 reissue.

culture.title: Placebo, 2016
culture.line: Placebo released it as a double A-side with 'Jesus' Son' and on an EP named after it. The Divine Comedy did a string-quartet version in 1994.

culture.title: James Marsh's cover art
culture.line: The single's sleeve is by James Marsh and the album credits list him for The Colour of Spring's cover illustration too.
